<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14810"/><div sID="gen28584" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14810"/><hi type="bold">32-34. They now tell each to the other how their hearts burned--</hi>were fired--within them at His talk and His expositions of Scripture. "Ah! <hi type="bold">this accounts for it: We could not understand the glow of self-evidencing light, love, glory that ravished our hearts; but now we do." They cannot rest--</hi>how could they?--they must go straight back and tell the news. They find the eleven, but ere they have time to tell their tale, their ears are saluted with the thrilling news, "The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon." Most touching and precious intelligence this. The only one of the Eleven to whom He appeared alone was he, it seems, who had so shamefully denied Him. What passed at that interview we shall never know here. Probably it was too sacred for disclosure. (See on <reference osisRef="Mark.16.7">Mr 16:7</reference>). The two from Emmaus now relate what had happened to them, and while thus comparing notes of their Lord's appearances, lo! Christ Himself stands in the midst of them. What encouragement to doubting, dark, true-hearted disciples! <div eID="gen28584" type="x-p"/>
